primary_claim: Across a benchmark of nine objective CoT-interpretability proxy tasks, non-LLM methods (linear/attention/SAE probes, TF-IDF) outperform LLM-based CoT monitors on 6 of 9 tasks out-of-distribution, including large advantages on predicting reasoning termination and Gemma's self-deletion, though no single method dominates across all tasks and some tasks (e.g. follow-up question response prediction) remain near-chance for all methods.

effect.metric: g-mean² (TPR x TNR) and AUC on binary classification tasks
effect.value: non-LLM methods outperform LLM monitors on 6/9 tasks OOD; e.g. reasoning-termination task: probes have OOD AUC>0.90 while LLM monitors perform worse than random OOD; follow-up question task: no method exceeds 0.48 g-mean² even in-distribution

stated_future_work: Address the confound in the follow-up-question task where methods must predict both the response and its effect on reported confidence (chain of predictions makes the task harder than necessary)
limitations_stated: Only tried GPT-5.2 at medium effort with several prompt iterations for LLM monitors; may not have the optimal prompt-model combination
Atypical-answer task sits close to chance for most methods; unclear whether this reflects subtle signal or genuinely no learnable signal
Follow-up question task confounds two sub-problems (predicting the response, then its effect on confidence), making it intrinsically hard
quote: We introduce and open source nine objective tasks, where a black box GPT 5.2 monitor falls short OOD. We also baseline probes (linear, attention, SAE) and text frequency analysis (TF-IDF), and find they often do better than zero-shot and few-shot LLM monitors OOD.
